qs.q: Which of the following is a minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies a tuple in a relation?
qs.e: A candidate key is a super key from which no attribute can be removed.

qs.q: Relation R(A, B, C, D) has exactly two candidate keys: {A} and {B, C}. How many super keys does R have?
qs.e: Sets containing A: 8. Sets containing B and C but not A: 2 (with or without D). Total = 10.

qs.q: For R(A, B, C, D) with functional dependencies A → B, B → C and C → D, the candidate key is:
qs.e: A determines B, then C, then D. So closure of A is the whole relation and A is minimal.

qs.q: For R(A, B, C, D, E) with AB → C, C → D and D → E, the candidate key is:
qs.e: A and B never appear on a right side, so both must be in the key. Closure of AB gives all attributes.

qs.q: R(A, B, C, D) has functional dependencies AB → C and C → A. How many candidate keys does R have?
qs.e: D and B are in every key. ABD and BCD both give the full closure. So there are 2 candidate keys.

qs.q: Attributes that are part of at least one candidate key are called:
qs.e: Prime attributes belong to some candidate key. The rest are non-prime.

qs.q: A foreign key in a child table must refer to:
o: An index of the child table
A column of the same row only
A view defined on the parent table
Any non-key column of the parent table
A primary key or unique key of the parent table
qs.e: A foreign key references a candidate key (primary or unique) of the parent relation.

qs.q: Which integrity rule states that no attribute of a primary key can be NULL?
qs.e: Entity integrity: primary key values must be unique and not NULL.

qs.q: Referential integrity between two tables is enforced using a:
qs.e: A foreign key value must match an existing parent key value or be NULL.

qs.q: A primary key made of two or more attributes is called a:
qs.e: Composite key = key with more than one column, for example (order_id, product_id).

qs.q: Candidate keys that are not selected as the primary key are called:
qs.e: One candidate key becomes primary. The others are alternate keys.

qs.q: A system-generated key with no business meaning, such as an auto-increment id, is called a:
qs.e: A surrogate key is artificial. A natural key comes from real data such as email or PAN.

qs.q: A relation has n attributes and its only candidate key is the single attribute A. The number of super keys is:
qs.e: Every super key must contain A. The other n−1 attributes are free, giving 2^(n−1) sets.

qs.q: Which statement about PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints in SQL is correct?
o: A table can have many PRIMARY KEY constraints
A UNIQUE constraint cannot cover two columns
A table can have many UNIQUE constraints but only one PRIMARY KEY
UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY are identical in all respects
A PRIMARY KEY column may hold one NULL
qs.e: Only one primary key per table. UNIQUE can be declared many times and normally allows NULL.

qs.q: The main purpose of normalization is to:
o: Reduce redundancy and avoid update anomalies
Increase redundancy to speed up queries
qs.e: Normalization splits tables so each fact is stored once.

qs.q: A relation is in First Normal Form (1NF) if:
o: Every attribute holds only atomic values
Every determinant is a super key
qs.e: 1NF: no repeating groups and no multi-valued cells.

qs.q: A relation in 1NF has a non-prime attribute that depends on only a part of a candidate key. Which normal form does it first fail to satisfy?
qs.e: Partial dependency breaks 2NF.

qs.q: Removing transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on the key takes a 2NF relation to:
qs.e: 3NF = 2NF + no transitive dependency of non-prime attributes.

qs.q: A relation is in BCNF if, for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y:
o: X and Y are both non-prime
qs.e: BCNF is stricter than 3NF. Every determinant must be a super key.

qs.q: Fourth Normal Form (4NF) is concerned with:
qs.e: 4NF removes non-trivial multivalued dependencies.

qs.q: Fifth Normal Form (5NF), also called Project-Join Normal Form, deals with:
qs.e: 5NF: every join dependency is implied by the candidate keys.

qs.q: R(A, B, C) has functional dependencies AB → C and C → B. The highest normal form of R is:
qs.e: Candidate keys are AB and AC, so all attributes are prime (3NF holds). C → B fails BCNF because C is not a super key.

qs.q: R(A, B, C, D) has candidate key AB and functional dependencies AB → C and B → D. The highest normal form of R is:
qs.e: B → D is a partial dependency (D depends on part of the key). So R is only in 1NF.

qs.q: R(A, B, C, D) has candidate key A and functional dependencies A → B, B → C and C → D. The highest normal form of R is:
qs.e: Single-attribute key means no partial dependency (2NF). B → C is transitive, so 3NF fails.

qs.q: A relation with exactly two attributes is always in:
qs.e: With two attributes, any non-trivial dependency has a key on the left side. So it is always in BCNF.

qs.q: If every attribute of a relation is a prime attribute, the relation is guaranteed to be in at least:
qs.e: 3NF allows X → A when A is prime. So an all-prime relation is always in 3NF.

qs.q: A relation in 1NF in which every candidate key is a single attribute is guaranteed to be in at least:
qs.e: Partial dependency needs a composite key. With simple keys it cannot occur.

qs.q: Which property of a decomposition guarantees that the original relation can be rebuilt by a natural join without extra tuples?
qs.e: Lossless (non-additive) join means no spurious tuples on joining.

qs.q: Up to which normal form can a relation always be decomposed with both lossless join and dependency preservation?
qs.e: 3NF synthesis always achieves both. BCNF may lose some dependencies.

qs.q: A decomposition into BCNF always guarantees:
o: Lossless join, but dependencies may not be preserved
Dependency preservation, but the join may be lossy
Neither lossless join nor dependency preservation
Both lossless join and dependency preservation
qs.e: The BCNF algorithm is lossless but can lose functional dependencies.

qs.q: If X → Y and Y → Z hold, then X → Z also holds. This inference rule is called:
qs.e: Transitivity is one of Armstrong's three basic axioms.

qs.q: If X → Y holds, then XZ → YZ also holds. This inference rule is called:
qs.e: Augmentation: adding the same attributes to both sides keeps the dependency.

qs.q: In R(A, B, C, D, E) with A → B, B → C and CD → E, the closure of {A} is:
qs.e: A gives B, B gives C. CD → E cannot fire because D is not in the closure.

qs.q: A functional dependency X → Y is called trivial when:
o: Y is a subset of X
X and Y have no common attribute
X is a subset of Y
qs.e: Example: AB → A is trivial. It holds in every relation.

qs.q: In Orders(order_id, product_id, product_name, supplier_city), details of a new product cannot be stored until someone orders it. This problem is called:
qs.e: Insertion anomaly: one fact cannot be inserted without another unrelated fact.

qs.q: In the same Orders table, deleting the only order of a product also removes the product's name and supplier city. This is called:
qs.e: Deletion anomaly: deleting one fact unintentionally removes another.

qs.q: Denormalization is mainly done to:
o: Improve read performance by reducing joins
qs.e: Denormalization adds controlled redundancy to make reports and reads faster.

qs.q: In the set of functional dependencies {A → B, B → C, A → C}, which dependency is redundant?
o: Both A → B and B → C
qs.e: A → C follows from A → B and B → C by transitivity, so it can be dropped from the minimal cover.

qs.q: The partial key of a weak entity set is also called its:
qs.e: A weak entity is identified by its discriminator plus the owner entity's key.

qs.q: When converting an ER diagram to tables, a many-to-many relationship is mapped to:
o: A single merged table of both entities
A foreign key in either one of the two tables
A separate table containing the primary keys of both entities
A view on the two tables
qs.e: Example: order_items(order_id, product_id) links orders and products.

qs.q: In an ER diagram, a key attribute is shown by:
qs.e: Underlined = key. Dashed ellipse = derived. Double ellipse = multivalued.

qs.q: A double ellipse in an ER diagram represents a:
qs.e: Example: a customer with several phone numbers.

qs.q: The number of tuples (rows) in a relation is called its:
qs.e: Cardinality = rows. Degree (arity) = columns.

qs.q: A foreign key is defined with ON DELETE CASCADE. What happens when a parent row is deleted?
o: Child foreign key values are set to default
Matching child rows are deleted automatically
Child foreign key values are set to NULL
qs.e: CASCADE propagates the delete to child rows. SET NULL and RESTRICT are other options.

qs.q: Which SQL statement is used to add a foreign key to an existing table?
o: ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY
qs.e: Constraints are added to existing tables with ALTER TABLE.

qs.q: A relation is in 3NF if, for every non-trivial functional dependency X → A:
o: X is a super key and A is non-prime only
X is a super key or A is a prime attribute
X and A are both non-prime
qs.e: 3NF relaxes BCNF by allowing the right side to be a prime attribute.

qs.q: A customers table stores several phone numbers in one column as "98110..., 98990...". Which normal form is violated?
qs.e: A cell must hold a single atomic value. A list in one cell breaks 1NF.

qs.q: Student(roll, name, dept_id, dept_name) has roll → name, dept_id and dept_id → dept_name. Which decomposition is in 3NF and lossless?
o: Student(roll, name, dept_id, dept_name) with no change
Student(roll, name, dept_name) and Dept(dept_id, roll)
Student(roll, name, dept_id) and Dept(dept_id, dept_name)
qs.e: Move the transitive part (dept_id → dept_name) to its own table and keep dept_id as the foreign key.

qs.q: Which of the following keys is allowed to contain NULL values?
qs.e: A foreign key may be NULL when the relationship is optional. Primary keys can never be NULL.

qs.q: R(A, B, C, D, E) has functional dependencies A → BC, CD → E, B → D and E → A. How many candidate keys does R have?
qs.e: The candidate keys are A, E, CD and BC. Each one's closure gives all five attributes.

qs.q: Ravi starts from his house and walks 12 m towards the east. Then he turns right and walks 24 m, turns left and walks 24 m, and finally turns right and walks 3 m. How far and in which direction is Ravi now from the starting point?
qs.e: Net movement: 36 m east and 27 m south. Distance = √(1296 + 729) = 45 m, direction South-East.

qs.q: The manager, along with his assistants, (A)/ were present at the meeting (B)/ which was held (C)/ at the head office. (D)
qs.e: The subject is "the manager" (singular). "Along with" does not make it plural. Use "was present".

qs.q: Neither the customers (A)/ nor the cashier (B)/ were aware of (C)/ the new rule. (D)
qs.e: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject "cashier". Use "was aware of".

qs.q: He has been working (A)/ in this branch (B)/ since five years (C)/ without taking any leave. (D)
qs.e: Use "for" with a period of time: "for five years". "Since" is used with a point of time.

qs.q: No sooner did the bell ring (A)/ when the students (B)/ rushed out (C)/ of the classroom. (D)
qs.e: "No sooner" is followed by "than", not "when".

qs.q: Each of the applicants (A)/ have submitted (B)/ the required documents (C)/ before the deadline. (D)
qs.e: "Each" takes a singular verb: "has submitted".

qs.q: One of my colleague (A)/ has been transferred (B)/ to the regional office (C)/ in Lucknow. (D)
qs.e: "One of" is followed by a plural noun: "one of my colleagues".

qs.q: Although he was tired, (A)/ but he completed (B)/ the audit report (C)/ before evening. (D)
qs.e: "Although" and "but" are not used together. Remove "but".

qs.q: She is one of the (A)/ most efficient officer (B)/ that the branch (C)/ has ever had. (D)
qs.e: "One of the" needs a plural noun: "most efficient officers".

qs.q: If I was you, (A)/ I would not (B)/ invest all my savings (C)/ in one scheme. (D)
qs.e: For an imaginary condition use "were": "If I were you".

qs.q: The number of digital transactions (A)/ have increased sharply (B)/ in rural areas (C)/ over the past two years. (D)
qs.e: "The number of" takes a singular verb: "has increased".

qs.q: He prefers (A)/ working in a village branch (B)/ than working (C)/ in a metro city. (D)
qs.e: "Prefer" is followed by "to", not "than".

qs.q: The new software is (A)/ more user-friendly (B)/ and faster than (C)/ the old one. (D)
qs.e: The sentence is correct.

qs.q: Hardly had the manager (A)/ left the cabin (B)/ than the phone (C)/ started ringing. (D)
qs.e: "Hardly" is followed by "when", not "than".

qs.q: She did not knew (A)/ that the account (B)/ had been frozen (C)/ by the bank. (D)
qs.e: After "did not" use the base form: "did not know".

qs.q: The RBI has decided to ______ the repo rate in order to control inflation.
qs.e: "Raise" takes an object (raise the rate). "Rise" does not take an object.

qs.q: The loan application was ______ because the applicant failed to provide income proof.
qs.e: "Rejected" means refused.

qs.q: Customers are advised not to ______ their OTP with anyone.
qs.e: "Share" means to give or tell to others.

qs.q: The branch manager was ______ of misusing customer funds.
qs.e: "Accused of" is the correct pair. We say "blamed for" and "charged with".

qs.q: The new policy will come into ______ from next month.
qs.e: "Come into effect" means to start to apply. "Affect" is a verb.

qs.q: Under the agreement, the guarantor is legally ______ to repay the loan if the borrower defaults.
qs.e: "Liable" means legally responsible.

qs.q: Despite ______ efforts by the technical staff, the server could not be restored.
qs.e: "Relentless" means continuous and determined, which fits with "despite".

qs.q: The bank ______ a notice to all defaulters last week.
qs.e: "Last week" needs the simple past tense: "issued".

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. He is too honest FOR ACCEPTING a bribe.
qs.e: The pattern is "too + adjective + to + verb".

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. This branch IS FUNCTIONING SINCE 1998.
qs.e: An action that started in the past and still continues takes the present perfect continuous.

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. I look forward TO MEET YOU next week.
qs.e: "Look forward to" is followed by the -ing form.

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. She IS KNOWING the answer.
qs.e: "Know" is a state verb and is not used in the continuous form.

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. The auditor asked him WHY WAS HE LATE.
qs.e: In reported questions the subject comes before the verb.

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. Unless you DO NOT SUBMIT the KYC documents, the account cannot be opened.
qs.e: "Unless" already means "if not", so it is not used with another negative.

qs.q: Choose the best replacement for the part in capitals. The cashier counted the notes CAREFULLY AND ACCURATELY.
qs.e: Two adverbs correctly describe the verb "counted". No change is needed.

qs.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRUDENT.
qs.e: Prudent means careful and sensible, especially with money.

qs.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to MITIGATE.
qs.e: Mitigate means to make something less severe.

qs.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.
qs.e: Abundant means available in large quantity.

qs.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT.
qs.e: Transparent means clear or open. Opaque means not clear.

qs.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.
qs.e: Diligent means hard-working.

qs.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to EXPAND.
qs.e: Expand means to grow larger. Contract means to become smaller.

qs.q: Which of the following should be the FIRST sentence after rearrangement?
qs.e: Correct order is B A C D E. (B) introduces the topic.
qs.ctx:
Rearrange the following five sentences (A), (B), (C), (D) and (E) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph, then answer the question.
(A) However, many villagers still travel long distances to reach a bank branch.
(B) Financial inclusion means giving every citizen access to basic banking services.
(C) To close this gap, banks appoint local agents called business correspondents.
(D) These agents carry handheld devices and offer deposits and withdrawals at the doorstep.
(E) As a result, even remote villages are slowly joining the formal banking system.

qs.e: Correct order is B A C D E. "As a result" in (E) gives the conclusion.

Rearrange the following five sentences (A), (B), (C), (D) and (E) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph, then answer the question.

qs.q: According to the passage, why were Regional Rural Banks set up?
o: To issue currency in rural areas
To serve small farmers, artisans and labourers neglected by large banks
To compete with foreign banks in cities
qs.e: The first sentence states this directly.
qs.ctx:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Regional Rural Banks were set up in 1975 to serve small farmers, artisans and labourers who were ignored by large commercial banks. For decades, these banks struggled with weak technology and high costs. Many branches kept records in paper ledgers, and customers waited days for a simple transfer. The situation began to change when the banks moved to core banking software. Today a farmer can check a balance on a basic mobile phone and receive a subsidy directly in the account. Yet technology alone does not solve every problem. Poor network coverage, low digital literacy and fear of fraud still keep many villagers away from digital channels. Experts therefore argue that banks must invest as much in training customers as they invest in machines.

qs.q: According to the passage, what began to change the situation of these banks?
o: The move to core banking software
qs.e: "The situation began to change when the banks moved to core banking software."

qs.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on:
qs.e: RBI started operations on 1 April 1935.

qs.q: The Reserve Bank of India was set up under which Act?
qs.e: The RBI Act, 1934 is the law that created the RBI.

qs.q: The RBI was established on the recommendation of which commission?
qs.e: The Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance) recommended a central bank in 1926.

qs.q: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised on:
qs.e: RBI was privately owned at first. It was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

qs.q: The central office of the RBI was first located in which city before it was moved to Mumbai in 1937?
qs.e: The central office started in Kolkata (then Calcutta) and moved to Mumbai in 1937.

qs.q: Who was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
qs.e: Sir Osborne Smith was Governor from 1935 to 1937.

qs.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
qs.e: C. D. Deshmukh became Governor in 1943.

qs.q: The accounting year of the RBI now runs from:
qs.e: RBI moved from a July–June year to April–March, aligning it with the government's financial year.

qs.q: What is the maximum number of Deputy Governors the RBI can have?
qs.e: The RBI Act allows up to four Deputy Governors.

qs.q: The Governor of the RBI is appointed by:
o: The Central Board of the RBI
The President of India on advice of the Chief Justice
qs.e: The Governor and Deputy Governors are appointed by the Central Government.

qs.q: The emblem of the Reserve Bank of India shows:
o: A peacock and a banyan tree
A tiger and a palm tree
qs.e: The RBI seal has a tiger standing before a palm tree.

qs.q: How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) have?
qs.e: Three members are from the RBI and three are appointed by the Central Government.

qs.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee?
o: The Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy
qs.e: The RBI Governor chairs the MPC.

qs.q: What is the quorum for a meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee?
qs.e: Four members must be present, and one of them must be the Governor (or the Deputy Governor in his absence).

qs.q: The MPC is required to meet at least how many times in a year?
qs.e: The law requires at least four meetings a year. In practice it meets every two months.

qs.q: If votes in the MPC are tied, the deciding vote is cast by:
qs.e: The Governor has a second or casting vote in case of a tie.

qs.q: Members of the MPC appointed by the Central Government hold office for:
o: 2 years and are not eligible for reappointment
6 years or up to the age of 65
3 years and may be reappointed once
4 years and are not eligible for reappointment
qs.e: External members serve a single four-year term.

qs.q: The inflation target given to the RBI under the flexible inflation targeting framework is:
qs.e: Target is 4% CPI inflation, with a tolerance band from 2% to 6%.

qs.q: The inflation target is set by:
o: The Central Government in consultation with the RBI
The Monetary Policy Committee by voting
qs.e: The government fixes the target once every five years after consulting the RBI. The MPC then sets the repo rate to achieve it.

qs.q: Which index is used by the RBI for inflation targeting?
qs.e: The headline CPI (Combined) is the nominal anchor.

qs.q: Which committee recommended the adoption of inflation targeting based on CPI in India?
qs.e: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) suggested CPI-based flexible inflation targeting.

qs.q: The repo rate is the rate at which:
o: The RBI lends short-term funds to banks against government securities
Banks borrow from each other overnight
The RBI lends long-term funds to state governments
Banks lend to their best customers
qs.e: Repo = repurchase agreement. Banks sell securities to the RBI and agree to buy them back.

qs.q: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) was introduced by the RBI in:
qs.e: SDF came in April 2022 and replaced the fixed rate reverse repo as the floor of the corridor.

qs.q: A key feature of the Standing Deposit Facility is that:
o: It replaces the cash reserve ratio
Banks borrow from the RBI without collateral
The RBI absorbs liquidity from banks without giving collateral
It is available only to cooperative banks
qs.e: Under SDF, banks park surplus funds with the RBI and the RBI gives no securities in return.

qs.q: Under the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), banks can:
o: Borrow from the RBI without any limit or collateral
Borrow long-term funds for priority sector lending
Borrow overnight from the RBI by dipping into their SLR securities
Lend to the RBI at the repo rate
Deposit surplus funds with the RBI for one year
qs.e: MSF is an emergency overnight window at a rate above the repo rate.

qs.q: The Marginal Standing Facility was introduced in the year:
qs.e: MSF started in May 2011.

qs.q: In the liquidity adjustment facility corridor, the ceiling rate is the:
qs.e: SDF is the floor, repo is the policy rate in the middle, and MSF is the ceiling.

qs.q: At present, the Bank Rate is aligned with which rate?
qs.e: The Bank Rate moves with the MSF rate. It is used to compute penalties on CRR and SLR shortfalls.

qs.q: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) was introduced on the recommendation of the:
o: Narasimham Committee on Banking Sector Reforms (1998)
qs.e: LAF was introduced in 2000 following the second Narasimham Committee.

qs.q: The operating target of India's monetary policy is the:
qs.e: The RBI tries to keep the WACR close to the repo rate.

qs.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio is calculated as a percentage of a bank's:
qs.e: CRR and SLR are both percentages of NDTL.

qs.q: Banks maintain the Cash Reserve Ratio in the form of:
o: Gold kept in their own vaults
Treasury bills kept with the SBI
qs.e: CRR is kept as a cash balance with the RBI.

qs.q: What interest does the RBI pay to banks on CRR balances?
o: Interest at the savings bank rate
qs.e: CRR balances earn nothing, so CRR is a cost for banks.

qs.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio is prescribed under:
qs.e: CRR comes from Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934.

qs.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio is prescribed under:
qs.e: SLR comes from Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an eligible asset for maintaining SLR?
qs.e: SLR is kept in cash, gold and approved government securities.

qs.q: As of November 2026, the CRR and SLR are respectively:
qs.e: CRR is 3.00% and SLR is 18.00% of NDTL.

qs.q: NDTL stands for:
qs.e: NDTL is roughly the deposits of a bank (demand + time) after netting inter-bank items.

qs.q: Open Market Operations refer to:
o: Auction of foreign currency by banks
Buying and selling of government securities by the RBI
Lending by banks to the open market
Sale of shares by banks in the stock market
qs.e: The RBI buys securities to add liquidity and sells them to absorb liquidity.

qs.q: When the RBI sells government securities in the open market, liquidity in the banking system:
qs.e: Buyers pay the RBI, so money leaves the system.

qs.q: To control high inflation, the RBI would normally:
qs.e: A higher repo rate makes loans costlier and reduces demand.

qs.q: Which of the following is a qualitative (selective) tool of credit control?
qs.e: Qualitative tools include moral suasion, margin requirements and credit rationing. The others are quantitative.

qs.q: A 'dear money policy' means a policy of:
qs.e: Dear money = credit is costly. It is used to fight inflation.

qs.q: Bonds under the Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS) are issued to:
o: Absorb excess liquidity from the system
qs.e: MSS was introduced in 2004 to mop up liquidity created by large foreign inflows.

qs.q: The Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) system came into effect from:
qs.e: MCLR replaced the base rate system from 1 April 2016.

qs.q: The one rupee note is issued by:
o: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
qs.e: The ₹1 note is issued by the government and signed by the Finance Secretary.

qs.q: Currency notes of ₹10 and above carry the signature of the:
qs.e: All notes issued by the RBI are signed by the Governor.

qs.q: India follows which system for the issue of currency notes?
qs.e: Under the Minimum Reserve System (since 1956) the RBI keeps ₹200 crore, of which ₹115 crore is in gold.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the RBI?
o: Acting as banker to the government
Accepting deposits from the general public
qs.e: The RBI does not deal with the public as a commercial bank does.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI?
qs.e: The RBI transferred its stake in NABARD to the Government of India. The other four are RBI subsidiaries.

sections.name: Computer Knowledge
sections.syllabus: Fundamentals, memory, networking, MS Office, security

qs.q: First generation computers were based on:
qs.e: 1st: vacuum tubes. 2nd: transistors. 3rd: ICs. 4th: microprocessors.

qs.q: Transistors were the main technology of which generation of computers?
qs.e: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes in the second generation.

qs.q: Integrated circuits (ICs) were first used in which generation of computers?
qs.e: Third generation computers used ICs.

qs.q: The microprocessor is associated with which generation of computers?
qs.e: Fourth generation: VLSI and microprocessors.

qs.q: Which part of the computer is known as its brain?
qs.e: The CPU carries out all instructions.

qs.q: Which of the following is the fastest type of memory?
qs.e: Speed order: register, cache, RAM, SSD, hard disk.

qs.q: Which of the following is non-volatile memory?
qs.e: ROM keeps its contents when power is off.

qs.q: Firmware is normally stored in:
qs.e: Firmware, such as the BIOS, lives in ROM or flash memory.

qs.q: Which memory loses its contents when the power is switched off?
qs.e: RAM is volatile.

qs.q: A group of 4 bits is called a:
qs.e: 4 bits = 1 nibble. 8 bits = 1 byte.

qs.q: 1 gigabyte (GB) is equal to:
An IPv4 address is how many bits long?
qs.e: IPv4 = 32 bits, written as four decimal numbers.

qs.q: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
qs.e: IPv6 = 128 bits, written in hexadecimal.

qs.q: A MAC address is how many bits long?
qs.e: A MAC (physical) address has 48 bits, shown as 12 hexadecimal digits.

qs.q: The default port number of POP3 is:
qs.e: POP3: 110. SMTP: 25. IMAP: 143.

qs.q: The default port number of HTTPS is:
qs.e: HTTP: 80. HTTPS: 443.

qs.q: Which protocol is used to send email from a client to a mail server?
qs.e: SMTP sends mail. POP3 and IMAP receive it.

qs.q: Which service translates a domain name into an IP address?
qs.e: DNS maps names like example.com to IP addresses. It uses port 53.

qs.q: In which topology is every node connected directly to every other node?
qs.e: A full mesh has a link between every pair of nodes.

qs.q: In which topology are all devices connected to a central hub or switch?
qs.e: Star topology uses a central device.

qs.q: A network that connects computers inside a single building is called a:
qs.e: LAN = Local Area Network.

qs.q: Which device works at the network layer and forwards packets between different networks?
qs.e: Routers use IP addresses (layer 3). Switches and bridges work at layer 2.

qs.q: Which of the following gives the safest connection over a public network?
qs.e: A VPN encrypts traffic between your device and the network.

qs.q: URL stands for:
qs.e: A URL is the address of a web page.

qs.q: The default file extension of a Microsoft Word 2016 document is:
qs.e: Word 2007 and later save as .docx by default.

qs.q: The default file extension of a Microsoft Excel 2016 workbook is:
qs.e: Excel 2007 and later save as .xlsx by default.

qs.q: The default slide orientation in Microsoft PowerPoint is:
qs.e: Slides are landscape by default. Word pages are portrait by default.

qs.q: Which shortcut key is used to undo the last action?
qs.e: Ctrl + Z undoes. Ctrl + Y redoes.

qs.q: In Microsoft Word, Ctrl + K is used to:
qs.e: Ctrl + K opens the Insert Hyperlink box.

qs.q: Which function key starts the spelling and grammar check in Microsoft Word?
qs.e: F7 runs the spell check. F12 opens Save As.

qs.q: In Microsoft PowerPoint, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
qs.e: F5 starts from the beginning. Shift + F5 starts from the current slide.

qs.q: Every formula in Microsoft Excel begins with which sign?
qs.e: A formula starts with the equals sign, for example =SUM(A1:A5).

qs.q: In Microsoft Excel, the intersection of a row and a column is called a:
qs.e: A cell is named by its column letter and row number, such as B4.

qs.q: Which Excel function counts the cells in a range that contain numbers?
qs.e: COUNT counts numeric cells. COUNTA counts all non-empty cells.

qs.q: In Microsoft Excel, pressing Ctrl + Home moves the cursor to:
o: The last row of the sheet
The start of the current row
qs.e: Ctrl + Home goes to A1. Ctrl + End goes to the last used cell.

qs.q: Linux is an example of:
qs.e: Linux is a free, open-source, multi-user operating system.

qs.q: MS-DOS is a:
qs.e: MS-DOS runs one user and one task at a time through typed commands.

qs.q: In a time-sharing operating system:
o: Each user gets a separate CPU
Only one program runs until it finishes
Programs run only at fixed clock times
CPU time is divided into small slices among many users
Jobs are collected and run in batches without interaction
qs.e: Each user gets a short time slice in turn, so everyone seems to be served at once.

qs.q: POST, which runs when a computer is switched on, stands for:
qs.e: POST checks the hardware before the operating system loads.

qs.q: Which key combination deletes a file permanently without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
qs.e: Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin.

qs.q: A Trojan horse is:
o: An email sent to many people
A program that copies itself across a network without help
A hardware fault in the hard disk
A harmful program disguised as useful software
A tool that speeds up the computer
qs.e: A Trojan pretends to be useful software. Unlike a virus or worm, it does not replicate itself.

qs.q: Malware that spreads from computer to computer over a network by copying itself, without attaching to a file, is called a:
qs.e: A worm is self-replicating and needs no host file.

qs.q: Sending fake emails that look like they come from a bank, in order to steal passwords, is called:
qs.e: Phishing tricks users into giving away confidential details.

qs.q: A firewall is used to:
o: Increase the speed of the internet
Filter incoming and outgoing network traffic
qs.e: A firewall blocks unauthorised access based on rules.

qs.q: The binary equivalent of the decimal number 13 is:
The decimal equivalent of the hexadecimal number 1F is:
Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code. How many characters can it represent?
qs.e: 2 to the power 7 = 128.

qs.q: Which translator converts a whole high-level program into machine code in one go?
qs.e: A compiler translates the full program. An interpreter works line by line.

qs.q: Which of the following is an input device?
qs.e: A scanner sends data into the computer. The others are output devices.

qs.q: The speed of a processor is measured in:
qs.e: Clock speed is given in hertz, usually GHz.
